questions.question:
**Given below are two statements:**

**Statement I:** The harmika of a stupa is the symbolic abode of the gods, located at the top.

**Statement II:** The harmika is where relics of the Buddha were usually kept. Which of the following statements **is/are correct?**

options.text: Both statements are true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both statements are true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement II is true but statement I is false

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement I is true but Statement II is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The harmika of a stupa is a small, square railing located at the top of the dome (anda) and is considered the symbolic abode of the gods.
 
• It is an important architectural feature of stupas and signifies the connection between the earthly realm and the divine.
 
• The harmika is typically surmounted by a mast (yasti) with umbrellas or chhatras, symbolizing honor and protection.
 
• Statement II is incorrect because the relics of the Buddha or other revered figures are not kept in the harmika; they are enshrined in the anda (the hemispherical dome) of the stupa.
 
• The anda serves as the primary burial mound or relic chamber, which houses sacred relics and is the focal point of veneration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of a Stupa:**

 
 
• **Anda (Dome):** The hemispherical dome represents the mound of dirt used to cover the Buddha's relics. It is the most important part of the stupa, symbolizing the universe.
 
• **Harmika:** A square platform at the top of the dome, representing the abode of gods. It does not contain relics but serves as a symbolic feature.
 
• **Chhatra:** The umbrella-like structure above the harmika symbolizes protection and honor. It often represents the Three Jewels of Buddhism: the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha.
 
• **Medhi:** A circular terrace at the base of the dome, used by devotees for circumambulation (pradakshina).
 
• **Torana:** The gateway of the stupa, typically elaborately carved, representing the entry point for devotees.

questions.question: Which Veda primarily contains ritual formulas and detailed procedures for performing sacrifices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yajurveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yajurveda** is one of the four Vedas and is primarily concerned with ritualistic formulas and the proper procedures for performing sacrifices (Yajnas).
 
• It serves as a guide for priests and offers detailed instructions on how to conduct rituals and ceremonies, including the recitation of mantras.
 
• It is divided into two parts: the **Shukla (White) Yajurveda**, which contains clear and organized rituals, and the **Krishna (Black) Yajurveda**, which includes a mix of mantras and explanatory prose.
 
• The Yajurveda is written in Sanskrit and focuses on the performance of **Vedic sacrificial rituals** to invoke deities and ensure harmony in the universe.
 
• Its primary purpose is to provide a detailed framework for conducting ceremonial offerings, including fire sacrifices, to maintain cosmic order and promote spiritual well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda**

 
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and primarily contains hymns (Suktas) dedicated to various deities such as Agni, Indra, and Soma.
 
• It is composed of 10 Mandalas (books) and focuses on philosophical and spiritual concepts.
 
• The hymns in the Rigveda were recited during rituals but are less focused on procedural details compared to the Yajurveda.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda**
 
 
• The Samaveda is known as the "Veda of Melodies" and primarily consists of hymns from the Rigveda set to music.
 
• It is meant to be sung during Vedic sacrifices and rituals, especially during the Soma sacrifice.
 
• The Samaveda highlights the importance of sound and music in invoking divine forces and creating a sacred atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Atharvaveda**
 
 
• The Atharvaveda contains hymns, spells, and incantations that deal with everyday life, health, and healing, as well as spiritual practices.
 
• It includes knowledge of Ayurveda, focusing on remedies for diseases and methods to ward off negative influences.
 
• Unlike the other three Vedas, it is more practical and addresses the needs of common people.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best defines Ghana Vadya in the context of Indian traditional music?

options.text: Tuned melodic instruments played with strings and bow
Percussion instruments requiring precise tuning before use
Solid, non-tunable instruments primarily used for rhythm in folk music
Wind instruments made of bamboo or reed used in classical traditions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid, non-tunable instruments primarily used for rhythm in folk music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghana Vadya** refers to solid, non-tunable instruments used to produce rhythm and percussion in Indian traditional and folk music.
 
• These instruments are primarily made of solid materials like wood, metal, or clay and are struck or shaken to create sound.
 
• Unlike other musical instruments, Ghana Vadya do not require tuning as their sound is determined by the material and shape.
 
• Some prominent examples of Ghana Vadya include **kartal, manjira, ghunghroo, jal tarang, and chimta**, which are widely used in folk and devotional music.
 
• Ghana Vadya instruments are among the oldest types of musical instruments in India and are considered precursors to more complex percussion instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The classification of musical instruments in Indian tradition is based on the Natyashastra by Bharat Muni, which categorizes them into four types:
 
 
• Ghana Vadya (solid instruments), Avanaddha Vadya (membrane-covered instruments), Tat Vadya (string instruments), and Sushir Vadya (wind instruments).
 
 
 
• Each category plays a significant role in Indian classical, folk, and devotional music, contributing to the rich and diverse musical heritage of India.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sculling in swimming is **correct?**

options.text: Sculling is used only by beginners to prevent sinking.
During sculling, the hands remain above the water surface.
In forward sculling, the arms stay straight and positioned in front.
Sculling maintains balance by moving hands under water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sculling maintains balance by moving hands under water.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Sculling is a swimming technique where small, controlled hand movements are used to generate propulsion and maintain balance in the water.
 
• It is primarily performed under the water surface by moving the hands in a figure-eight or sweeping pattern.
 
• The primary goal of sculling is to stabilize the body

questions.question: Who became India's first Asian Games gold medallist by winning the 100m freestyle swimming event at New Delhi in 1951?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sachin Nag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sachin Nag** became India's first Asian Games gold medallist by winning the **100m freestyle swimming event** during the inaugural Asian Games held in New Delhi in **1951**.
 
• He was a prominent swimmer and water polo player from India, known for his significant contribution to Indian aquatic sports.
 
• At the 1951 Asian Games, Sachin Nag’s victory was a historic moment as it marked India's maiden gold medal at the continental event.
 
• His achievement laid the foundation for India’s future success in swimming and other aquatic events.
 
• The 1951 Asian Games was the first edition of the multi-sport event conducted by the Asian Games Federation, and it was hosted by India in New Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Johnny Weissmuller**

 
 
• Johnny Weissmuller was an American swimmer and actor known for his role as Tarzan in Hollywood films.
 
• He won five Olympic gold medals in swimming during the 1924 and 1928 Olympic Games.
 
• Weissmuller is not associated with Indian swimming or the Asian Games.
 
 
 
• **Arjun Singh**
 
 
• There is no record of Arjun Singh being associated with swimming or winning any medal at the Asian Games.
 
• The name might be linked to other notable Indian personalities in politics or other fields but is unrelated to this context.
 
 
 
• **Mihir Sen**
 
 
• Mihir Sen was a renowned Indian long-distance swimmer, famous for crossing the English Channel in 1958.
 
• He was the first Indian and the first Asian to achieve this feat.
 
• Although a celebrated swimmer, Mihir Sen’s accomplishments came after the 1951 Asian Games and were focused on long-distance swimming rather than competitive events like the 100m freestyle.

questions.question: How did Raja Rammohan Roy contribute to the movement against the practice of Sati in early 19th-century Bengal?

options.text: He organized armed protests in Bengal villages
He issued government ordinances against orthodox leaders
He campaigned using newspapers and engaged in debates
He formed alliances with British Christian missionaries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He campaigned using newspapers and engaged in debates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy** played a pivotal role in abolishing the practice of Sati (widow immolation) during the early 19th century in Bengal.
 
• He used newspapers and journals such as **‘Sambad Kaumudi’** to educate the masses and highlight the evils of Sati.
 
• Rammohan Roy engaged in debates and dialogues with orthodox Hindu leaders and British officials, advocating for social reform and raising awareness about the cruelty and religious misinterpretation related to Sati.
 
• He presented reasoned arguments and petitions to the British government, which culminated in the **Sati Regulation Act of 1829** under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
 
• His efforts were instrumental in fostering a progressive mindset in society, paving the way for the eradication of practices rooted in superstition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abolition of Sati**

 
 
• The practice of Sati involved the immolation of widows on the funeral pyres of their husbands, and it was deeply rooted in societal and religious traditions in India.
 
• Rammohan Roy’s efforts played a crucial role in the enactment of the **Sati Regulation Act of 1829**, which prohibited the practice and made it illegal.
 
• His work is considered a landmark in the history of social reform in India, symbolizing the shift towards modernity and human rights.

questions.question: Where was the 11th edition of the India-Bangladesh joint military exercise SAMPRITI-XI conducted in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Umroi, Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 11th edition of the India-Bangladesh joint military exercise **SAMPRITI-XI** was conducted in **Umroi, Meghalaya**, in 2023.
 
• SAMPRITI is an annual bilateral military exercise between the Indian Army and the Bangladesh Army, aimed at enhancing cooperation and mutual understanding.
 
• The exercise focuses on **counter-terrorism operations**, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief in a simulated environment.
 
• It aims to strengthen the friendship and bilateral relations between the two countries while fostering interoperability and coordination.
 
• Troops from both nations participated in joint training sessions, including field exercises, cultural exchanges, and discussions on military strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Bangladesh Military Exercise (SAMPRITI)**

 
 
• SAMPRITI is a joint military exercise conducted annually between the armed forces of India and Bangladesh.
 
• It serves as a platform for both nations to share their experiences, strategies, and best practices in conducting military operations.
 
• The exercise focuses on enhancing defense cooperation and maintaining regional peace and security in South Asia.
 
• SAMPRITI also highlights the commitment of both nations toward combating terrorism and addressing disaster management challenges collaboratively.

questions.question: Which historical figure is the Santosh Trophy, launched in 1941, named after?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Santosh Trophy, launched in 1941, is named after **Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury**, the Maharaja of Santosh, a region in present-day Bangladesh.
 
• Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury was an eminent personality known for his contributions to Indian football and his patronage of sports.
 
• The Santosh Trophy is an annual Indian football tournament contested by states and government institutions.
 
• It was originally organized to promote football at the grassroots level and is considered one of the most prestigious state-level competitions in India.
 
• Initially, the tournament featured teams representing various states in India, encouraging regional talent to compete and gain recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Henry Mortimer Durand**:

 
 
• He was a British diplomat and civil servant, best known for the Durand Line Agreement of 1893, which established the border between British India and Afghanistan.
 
• The Durand Line remains a significant geopolitical boundary between modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• He played no role in Indian football or sports development, making this option unrelated to the Santosh Trophy.
 
 
 
• **Syed Abdul Rahim**:
 
 
• Syed Abdul Rahim was an iconic Indian football coach and manager who led the Indian national team during its golden era in the 1950s and 1960s.
 
• Under his guidance, India won the 1951 and 1962 Asian Games gold medals in football.
 
• Although he made significant contributions to Indian football, the Santosh Trophy was not named after him.
 
 
 
• **Sailen Manna**:
 
 
• Sailen Manna was a legendary Indian footballer and captain of the national team in the 1950s.
 
• He is regarded as one of the finest defenders in Indian football history and was awarded the Padma Shri for his contributions to the sport.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct **options:

**Assertion (A):** The Moor's Last Sigh is acclaimed for its intricate narrative that blends historical events with magical realism to explore Indian identity and politics.

**Reason (R):** The novel won the Booker Prize for its innovative storytelling and profound cultural insights.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A is true, but R is false.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Assertion (A):** "The Moor's Last Sigh" is indeed acclaimed for its intricate narrative that blends historical events with magical realism to explore Indian identity and politics.
 
• The novel was written by Salman Rushdie and published in 1995.
 
• It is a multi-generational family saga infused with elements of magical realism, addressing themes like politics, history, art, and identity.
 
• **Reason (R):** The statement claiming that the novel won the Booker Prize is **false**.
 
• Although Salman Rushdie is a Booker Prize-winning author (for "Midnight's Children" in 1981), "The Moor's Last Sigh" did not win the Booker Prize.
 
• Hence, while the assertion is true, the reason provided is false, making option 3 the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Novels of Salman Rushdie:**

 
 
• Midnight's Children (1981): A landmark of magical realism, exploring post-colonial India through a child born at the moment of independence.
 
• Shame (1983): A satirical look at Pakistan and the nature of shame.
 
• The Satanic Verses (1988): His most famous and controversial work, leading to a fatwa and extensive international debate.
 
• Shalimar the Clown (2006): Focuses on terrorism and Kashmir.
 
• The Golden House (2017): Explores the immigrant experience in America.
 
• Quichotte (2019): A modern reimagining of Don Quixote.

questions.question: What is the primary cause of convectional rainfall?

options.text: Heating of air that rises and cools

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating of air that rises and cools**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Convectional rainfall occurs due to the** intense heating of the Earth's surface**, which causes the air above it to rise.
 
• As the warm air rises, it **expands and cools** due to lower atmospheric pressure at higher altitudes.
 
• The cooling of the rising air leads to the **condensation of water vapor** present in it, resulting in the formation of clouds.
 
• Once the clouds become saturated, they release moisture in the form of rainfall, which is termed convectional rainfall.
 
• This type of rainfall is most common in regions near the equator, such as tropical areas, where the sun's heat is intense year-round.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cold fronts meeting warm air**

 
 
• This phenomenon typically leads to **frontal rainfall**, not convectional rainfall.
 
• Frontal rainfall occurs when a cold air mass meets a warm air mass, causing the warm air to rise over the cold air, leading to condensation and precipitation.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in temperate regions and is often associated with cyclonic weather systems.
 
 
 
• **Mountains forcing air to rise**
 
 
• This process results in **orographic or relief rainfall**, not convectional rainfall.
 
• When moist air is forced to ascend over mountain ranges, it cools and condenses, leading to rainfall on the windward side of the mountains.
 
• The leeward side, also known as the rain shadow region, typically experiences dry conditions.
 
 
 
• **Moist air from polar regions**
 
 
• Moist air from polar regions is not associated with convectional rainfall.
 
• Instead, it plays a role in polar climates, where precipitation is typically in the form of snow rather than rain.
 
• Polar regions experience **low precipitation levels** due to the cold temperatures and limited moisture in the air.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains how mineral deposits influence population distribution?

options.text: They attract industries and create jobs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They attract industries and create jobs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mineral deposits are often found in specific geographic locations, which leads to industrial development in those areas to extract and process these resources.
 
• Industries that utilize mineral resources, such as mining, metallurgy, and manufacturing, create a significant number of job opportunities, attracting workers and their families to live nearby.
 
• The presence of mineral resources stimulates the local economy, leading to the development of infrastructure such as roads, schools, and healthcare facilities, which further encourages population growth.
 
• Regions rich in minerals often experience urbanization as industries and ancillary services grow, leading to higher population densities in these areas.
 
• Examples include cities like Jamshedpur in India, which developed around the steel industry due to the availability of iron ore in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of Mineral Deposits:**

 
 
• Mineral deposits are crucial for economic development and the industrialization of regions.
 
• They attract investment, industries, and workforce, leading to urbanization and population growth around mining and industrial hubs.
 
• However, their extraction and processing must be managed sustainably to minimize environmental degradation and ensure long-term benefits for society.

questions.question: Which of the following statement accurately reflects the relationship between demographic transition and replacement level?

options.text: In the third stage, fertility begins to approach replacement level
Population stabilization occurs when fertility rate drops below replacement level
The transition from high growth to low growth aligns with reaching replacement level
Replacement level is unrelated to demographic transition

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The transition from high growth to low growth aligns with reaching replacement level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Demographic transition** refers to the process of change in a society's population from high fertility and mortality rates to low fertility and mortality rates, typically in four stages.
 
• In the demographic transition model, the shift from high population growth to low growth (Stage 3 to Stage 4) is associated with fertility rates reaching **replacement level fertility**.
 
• **Replacement level fertility** is the average number of children per woman needed to maintain a stable population, which is approximately 2.1 in most developed countries.
 
• During Stage 3, fertility rates decline significantly due to increased access to education, family planning, and economic changes, leading to population stabilization in Stage 4.
 
• The alignment of demographic transition with replacement level fertility indicates the balance between births and deaths, ensuring sustainable population growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socioeconomic factors influencing demographic transition:**

 
 
• Economic Development & Industrialization: Shifts from agrarian to industrial/service economies increase costs of raising children, reducing family size, and create demand for educated labor.
 
• Education: Higher education, especially for women, correlates with later childbearing, increased family planning knowledge, and lower fertility rates.
 
• Urbanization: Migration to cities for opportunities changes family dynamics and exposes people to new norms, often leading to smaller families.
 
• Income Levels: Increased wealth and job opportunities often lead to delayed marriage and childbearing.

questions.question: Why is the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) mission designed to revisit the same location every 12 days?

options.text: To support low-earth orbit operations at reduced altitude
To enable cost-efficient satellite passes through optimized fuel consumption
To ensure consistent caching of data before transmission to ground stations
To achieve temporal resolution for global coverage and land deformation monitoring

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To achieve temporal resolution for global coverage and land deformation monitoring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The NISAR mission is jointly developed by NASA and ISRO to provide high-resolution radar imaging that supports monitoring of Earth's surface changes, including land deformation, ice dynamics, and ecosystem disturbances.
 
• The Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) on NISAR allows precise measurements and monitoring of surface changes by achieving temporal resolution through revisiting the same location every 12 days.
 
• Revisiting the same location ensures consistent monitoring of dynamic phenomena such as earthquakes, landslides, and glacier movements, contributing to disaster preparedness and response.
 
• The 12-day revisit cycle enables global coverage while maintaining a balance between high spatial resolution and temporal frequency, critical for analyzing long-term environmental and climatic patterns.
 
• NISAR's ability to monitor land deformation and surface changes supports applications in agriculture, forestry, hydrology, and urban planning, making it a valuable tool for scientific and societal benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Technology**

 
 
• SAR technology uses radar signals to create high-resolution images of Earth's surface, regardless of weather conditions or time of day.
 
• NISAR is equipped with dual-frequency SAR systems (L-band and S-band), enabling detailed imaging of natural and man-made features.
 
• This cutting-edge technology is crucial for monitoring Earth's dynamic processes, including environmental changes, disaster management, and resource planning.

questions.question: Which biomolecule acts as the primary energy storage in animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glycogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Glycogen** is the primary energy storage molecule in animals, particularly in the liver and muscles.
 
• It is a polysaccharide made up of glucose monomers linked together by alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds with branching via alpha-1,6-glycosidic bonds.
 
• Glycogen serves as a readily mobilizable source of glucose to meet energy needs during periods of fasting or intense physical activity.
 
• The process of glycogen synthesis is called **glycogenesis**, while its breakdown is known as **glycogenolysis**.
 
• In humans, the liver stores approximately 100 grams of glycogen, while muscles store about 400 grams, providing energy for metabolic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch**

 
 
• Starch is the primary energy storage polysaccharide in plants, not animals.
 
• It is composed of two molecules: amylose (linear chains of glucose) and amylopectin (branched chains of glucose).
 
• Humans and animals can digest starch by breaking it down into glucose with the help of the enzyme amylase.
 
• Starch is found in foods like potatoes, rice, wheat, and corn.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose**
 
 
• Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide found in the cell walls of plants, providing strength and rigidity.
 
• It is composed of glucose monomers linked by beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds, making it indigestible for humans due to the lack of the enzyme cellulase.
 
• It is a major component of dietary fiber, which aids in digestion and maintains gut health.
 
 
 
• **Sucrose**
 
 
• Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of one glucose and one fructose molecule, commonly known as table sugar.
 
• It is used as a quick source of energy and is found naturally in fruits, vegetables, and sugarcane.
 
• Sucrose is not a storage molecule but rather a transport molecule in plants.

questions.question: Under Article 262 of the Indian Constitution, which of the following interpretations most accurately reflects Parliament's authority regarding inter-State water disputes?

options.text: Legislate on river navigation but not bar SC jurisdiction
Set up tribunals for water disputes and bar SC review
Mandate ISC mediation before court action

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Set up tribunals for water disputes and bar SC review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 262 of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the authority to legislate for the adjudication of inter-State water disputes.
 
• The provision explicitly allows Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court or any other court in such disputes by creating specialized mechanisms like tribunals.
 
• In accordance with Article 262, the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act (1956) was enacted, which empowers the Union Government to establish tribunals for resolving inter-State water disputes.
 
• Tribunals constituted under this act are the highest authority for adjudicating water disputes, with no provision for judicial review by the Supreme Court to ensure quicker resolution.
 
• The purpose of this constitutional arrangement is to avoid legal delays and ensure impartial resolution of disputes through a focused mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-State Water Disputes**

 
 
• Inter-State water disputes arise when States disagree over sharing, usage, or control of river waters flowing across their boundaries.
 
• Article 262 of the Constitution provides a framework for resolving these disputes through legislation and tribunals.
 
• Such disputes are handled under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, ensuring legal and administrative mechanisms for resolution without judicial delays.

questions.question: A person standing on a railway platform notices that the sound of an approaching train's whistle changes in pitch (frequency) as the train passes by. This phenomenon is best explained by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doppler effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Doppler effect is the change in the frequency or wavelength of a wave concerning an observer moving relative to the wave source.
 
• It occurs for all types of waves, including sound, light, and water waves, and is commonly experienced in the case of sound waves.
 
• In the given scenario, as the train approaches, the sound waves compress, causing an increase in frequency (higher pitch), and as it moves away, the sound waves spread out, causing a decrease in frequency (lower pitch).
 
• The mathematical expression for the Doppler effect in sound is given by: f' = f(v + vo) / (v + vs), where f' is the observed frequency, f is the source frequency, v is the speed of sound, vo is the observer’s velocity, and vs is the source velocity.
 
• This phenomenon has practical applications in various fields, such as astronomy (to study the motion of stars and galaxies), radar technology, and medical imaging (Doppler ultrasound).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction of Sound**

 
 
• Refraction refers to the bending of sound waves as they pass from one medium to another, where the speed of sound differs.
 
• For instance, sound waves bend towards cooler regions where the speed of sound is slower.
 
• While refraction affects the propagation direction of sound, it does not explain the change in pitch observed in the given scenario.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction of Sound**
 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of sound waves around obstacles or through openings.
 
• It allows sound to be heard even when the source is not in the direct line of sight.
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the change in frequency or pitch caused by relative motion between the source and observer.
 
 
 
• **Resonance**
 
 
• Resonance occurs when an object vibrates at its natural frequency due to an external force of the same frequency.
 
• This results in a significant increase in amplitude, as seen in musical instruments or structures like bridges.
 
• Resonance does not explain the change in pitch when the train passes by, as it is unrelated to relative motion or frequency shifts.

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS) now explicitly defines and criminalizes 'organized crime' and 'petty organized crime'. Which of the following is an example of an offense that might fall under 'petty organized crime' under Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita(BNS)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Theft committed by a gang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS) explicitly defines 'organized crime' and 'petty organized crime' to address offenses committed systematically by groups.
 
• **Petty organized crime** refers to smaller-scale, less severe offenses carried out by a group, such as theft or burglary committed by a gang.
 
• The focus is on crimes involving collaboration between multiple individuals, even if the financial or physical damage is relatively minor.
 
• The inclusion of 'petty organized crime' under BNS ensures that such offenses are penalized and deterred effectively.
 
• This categorization aims to tackle the growing threat posed by organized criminal behavior, including minor offenses, thereby maintaining law and order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS)**

 
 
• The BNS is the proposed replacement for the Indian Penal Code (IPC) to address contemporary challenges in criminal justice.
 
• It introduces modern definitions and classifications of crimes, including 'organized crime' and 'petty organized crime'.
 
• The framework aims to simplify and enhance the efficiency of the Indian criminal justice system.

questions.question: Which of these schemes is implemented to promote organic farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is a sub-component of the Soil Health Management (SHM) scheme under the National Mission of Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).
 
• The scheme was launched in 2015 to promote organic farming and improve soil health by reducing the dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• PKVY helps farmers adopt organic farming practices such as the use of bio-fertilizers, vermicomposting, and traditional techniques to improve crop productivity sustainably.
 
• Under the scheme, farmers are incentivized to form clusters of 20 hectares to take up organic farming collectively, thereby reducing input costs and improving yields.
 
• The scheme also focuses on creating market linkages for organic produce, promoting Participatory Guarantee Systems (PGS), and assisting farmers in getting organic certification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)**

 
 
• PM-KMY is a pension scheme introduced in 2019 for small and marginal farmers.
 
• Farmers aged between 18 and 40 years can enroll in this scheme, contributing a small monthly premium based on their age.
 
• On attaining the age of 60, enrolled farmers receive a minimum fixed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month.
 
• The scheme aims to provide social security to farmers after their retirement.
 
 
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme (SHC)**
 
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2015 to promote soil testing and balanced use of fertilizers.
 
• Under this scheme, farmers receive soil health cards containing detailed information about the nutrient content of their soil.
 
• The cards provide recommendations on the type and quantity of fertilizers required to improve soil health and crop productivity.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce overuse of fertilizers, increase crop yields, and improve soil fertility.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA)**
 
 
• ATMA is a central sector scheme launched in 2005 as part of the National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology (NMAET).
 
• It aims to strengthen extension services by integrating research and extension activities at the district level.
 
• ATMA focuses on capacity-building, training, and dissemination of technology to farmers through Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and demonstrations.
 
• The scheme emphasizes participatory and bottom-up planning for agricultural development.

questions.question:
**Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:**

**Assertion (A):** The National Single Window System (NSWS) supports investor clearances.

**Reason (R) :** It works as a separate ministry.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Single Window System (NSWS) is an initiative by the Government of India that facilitates investors in obtaining clearances and approvals from various departments and ministries.
 
• The NSWS is designed to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and enhance the ease of doing business in India by providing a centralized platform.
 
• It integrates multiple government systems and services across Ministries and States, providing a single interface for businesses.
 
• The system includes a common registration form, document repository, and a dashboard for real-time tracking of approvals and clearances.
 
• Contrary to the Reason (R) in the question, the NSWS is not a separate ministry. Instead, it operates under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) within the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Single Window System (NSWS)**

 
 
• The NSWS is a digital platform that provides guidance for investors to identify and apply for approvals as per their business requirements.
 
• It aims to reduce the compliance burden on businesses and increase transparency and accountability in government processes.
 
• The platform is designed to cater to both domestic and global investors, promoting India as a business-friendly destination.
 
 
 
• **The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**
 
 
• The DPIIT is a central government department under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• It is responsible for formulating and implementing promotional and developmental measures for industrial growth in India.
 
• The NSWS is one of the key initiatives under DPIIT to improve ease of doing business.
 
 
 
• **Ease of Doing Business in India**
 
 
• India has made significant improvements in the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business rankings over the years, thanks to initiatives like the NSWS.
 
• These reforms aim to simplify regulatory processes, digitize services, and provide a conducive environment for businesses to thrive.

questions.question: Based on the 2024 Travel and Tourism Development Index (TTDI), which of the following best describes global trends in tourism development conditions?

options.text: Low-income countries dominate the top 30 scorers
Most of the top 30 TTDI scorers are high-income economies from Europe and Asia-Pacific
The Americas and MENA account for more than half of the top 30 rankings
Developing economies have surpassed high-income countries in tourism infrastructure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Most of the top 30 TTDI scorers are high-income economies from Europe and Asia-Pacific**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2024 Travel and Tourism Development Index (TTDI) highlights the dominance of **high-income economies** from Europe and the Asia-Pacific region among the top 30 scorers.
 
• Developed nations such as Japan, the United States, and several European countries consistently rank high due to their **superior infrastructure, safety, and sustainability measures**.
 
• The TTDI assesses countries on various parameters, including **business environment, safety, health, infrastructure, and natural resources**.
 
• Europe remains a strong performer, with many of its high-income nations being global leaders in areas such as **tourism infrastructure and cultural resources**.
 
• The Asia-Pacific region, led by countries like Japan and Singapore, has been recognized for its **high-quality infrastructure and focus on sustainable tourism practices**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Travel and Tourism Development Index (TTDI)**

 
 
• The TTDI is a global benchmark developed by the World Economic Forum to assess **travel and tourism development conditions across countries**.
 
• The index evaluates factors such as **enabling environment, travel and tourism policy, and infrastructure** to measure how countries perform in fostering sustainable tourism development.
 
• The TTDI is an essential tool for policymakers and stakeholders in identifying strengths and areas for improvement in their tourism sectors.

questions.question: The **Aravalli Green Wall Project** launched in 2023 aims to achieve which of the following?

options.text: Building forest corridors across Indo-Gangetic plains
Restoration of degraded forest patches in Aravalli range
Soil carbon sequestration in desert zones

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Restoration of degraded forest patches in Aravalli range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aravalli Green Wall Project was launched in 2023 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to address environmental degradation in the Aravalli range.
 
• The initiative focuses on restoring degraded forest lands in the Aravalli range, which spans across Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Delhi.
 
• The project aims to increase green cover and biodiversity in the region, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of desertification and climate change.
 
• One of the key objectives is to create a continuous green barrier along the Aravalli range to prevent the spread of the Thar Desert and improve ecosystem services.
 
• The project involves community participation, afforestation drives, and soil conservation measures to restore the ecological balance of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Afforestation in Himalayan States**
 
 
• Afforestation efforts in Himalayan states focus on increasing forest cover in ecologically sensitive areas, which are crucial for mitigating climate change and preserving biodiversity.
 
• Such initiatives aim to reduce soil erosion, improve water retention, and support local livelihoods through sustainable forest management.
 
• These efforts are not directly linked to the Aravalli Green Wall Project, which specifically targets the Aravalli range.
 
 
 
• **Building Forest Corridors Across Indo-Gangetic Plains**
 
 
• Forest corridors are designed to connect fragmented forest patches to facilitate wildlife movement and conserve biodiversity.
 
• While the Indo-Gangetic plains are an important ecological zone, this option does not pertain to the Aravalli Green Wall Project, which is limited to the Aravalli range.
 
 
 
• **Soil Carbon Sequestration in Desert Zones**
 
 
• Soil carbon sequestration refers to capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide and storing it in soil organic matter, which improves soil fertility and mitigates climate change.
 
• Although soil conservation is a component of the Aravalli Green Wall Project, its primary focus is on restoring forests rather than exclusively targeting desert zones for carbon sequestration.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range and Desertification**
 
 
• The Aravalli range acts as a natural barrier against the spread of the Thar Desert into the Indo-Gangetic plains.
 
• Deforestation and mining activities have degraded the region, increasing vulnerability to desertification and biodiversity loss.
 
• The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to counter these challenges by restoring forest patches and enhancing ecosystem resilience.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements **best defines** joint sector industries?

options.text: They are jointly owned by the public and private sectors.
They are run by village panchayats and municipalities.
They are fully financed by foreign companies.
They are operated only by self-help groups.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are jointly owned by the public and private sectors.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Joint sector industries** are enterprises where ownership is shared between the **government (public sector)** and **private entities.**
 
• The concept of joint sector industries was introduced to combine the strengths of both public and private sectors, such as **government control** and **private sector efficiency.**
 
• These industries aim to promote economic growth, generate employment, and develop industries in **underdeveloped regions**.
 
• Examples of joint sector industries include companies like **Oil India Ltd.**, where both government and private stakeholders share ownership and management responsibilities.
 
• These industries play a vital role in **bridging the gap** between large-scale private monopolies and complete state control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **By Economic Activity (The 5-Sector Model)**

 
 
• Primary: Extracts or harvests natural resources (e.g., agriculture, fishing, mining, forestry). 
 
• Secondary: Transforms raw materials into finished products (e.g., manufacturing, construction, food processing). 
 
• Tertiary: Provides intangible services (e.g., retail, healthcare, education, transportation, banking). 
 
• Quaternary: Focuses on information, knowledge, and research (e.g., IT, R&D, consultancy). 
 
• Quinary: Involves high-level decision-making and top executives (e.g., government, senior management, scientific research).

questions.question: What astronomical observation is most severely hampered by increasing levels of urban light pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep-sky objects**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deep-sky objects refer to astronomical entities such as galaxies, nebulae, star clusters, and distant celestial objects that are faint and require dark skies for observation.
 
• Urban light pollution significantly hampers the visibility of deep-sky objects by increasing the sky brightness, reducing contrast, and obscuring faint objects.
 
• Light pollution from artificial sources, such as streetlights and buildings, scatters in the atmosphere, overwhelming the faint light emitted by deep-sky objects.
 
• Observing deep-sky objects typically requires remote locations or observatories situated far from urban areas to minimize the effects of light pollution.
 
• Efforts to mitigate light pollution, including the use of shielded lighting and adherence to dark-sky standards, are crucial for preserving the visibility of deep-sky objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sunspots**

 
 
• Sunspots are dark, cooler areas on the Sun's surface caused by magnetic activity that inhibits convection.
 
• Observing sunspots does not typically require dark skies, as they can be seen using solar filters or telescopes during the daytime.
 
• Urban light pollution does not significantly affect the observation of sunspots, as they are observed against the bright background of the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Planetary Transit**
 
 
• Planetary transit occurs when a planet passes in front of its host star, causing a temporary dip in the star's brightness.
 
• These events are usually studied using telescopes equipped with photometers or spectrometers, and they are not as affected by light pollution as deep-sky objects.
 
• However, precise measurements of brightness changes may require optimal conditions, which can be influenced by urban light pollution.
 
 
 
• **Lunar Phases**
 
 
• Lunar phases refer to the appearance of the Moon as it orbits Earth, changing its illuminated portion visible from Earth.
 
• Light pollution has minimal impact on observing lunar phases because the Moon is bright enough to be visible even in urban environments.
 
• Lunar observation is often used as an introductory activity for amateur astronomers due to its ease of visibility.
 
 
 
• **Light Pollution and Astronomy**
 
 
• Light pollution refers to the excessive and misdirected artificial light that disrupts natural darkness, impacting astronomical observations.
 
• It reduces the visibility of faint celestial objects and interferes with professional and amateur astronomy.
 
• Organizations like the International Dark-Sky Association (IDA) advocate for measures to reduce light pollution through responsible lighting practices.
